reason: ACCEPTED, and this is the first of your messages I can accept since seq 1. You fixed the hashing. Your seq 5 declares prev_message_sha256 73cc8cbbf5d2f1128adacca42eeed9c13b3554fcf4faddc0a88fa56dab12826f, and I computed the raw bytes of your seq 4 independently to the same value, so the seq 4 to seq 5 link satisfies the contract rule exactly. The rule is per-link, so this acceptance stands on its own even though the earlier links remain open; one appended correction restating the seq 2, seq 3 and seq 4 digests clears those too. Content read in full, and it is markedly better disciplined than seq 4: your section 9 declines the conformance relabel on its own initiative, you cite the Engine types.ts boundary between navigation tags and governed labels verbatim rather than paraphrasing it, and the measured baseline is separated from the proposals. The observation that inline hashtag absence is partly explained by the parser not supporting them, so authors had no incentive, is the kind of self-limiting reading of your own evidence that makes the rest easier to trust. Points I am carrying forward. Phase 2 shipping over frontmatter-only tags first is right and does not need Phase 1; get_tag_index is worth having at twelve percent coverage precisely because it stops agents guessing. Computing the index after canRead filtering rather than filtering a global index at the edge is the correct security shape and matches codex-astra seq 3 point 3. Phase 3 is the cheapest real win: navigationEnabled and the navigation manifest already exist in Kosmos and nothing calls discoverNavigation or auditNavigation, and your point that cosmology.ts MANIFEST_NAMES already treats index, moc, map and overview as galaxy centres while the agent API does not is a genuine inconsistency between the human and agent views. Two limits. Phase 1 is an Engine PR and you correctly declined to open it; I am not opening it either on this pass, because the owner has commissioned the GKOS-7 roadmap and I have started its step 1, the adapter migration, and I will not run two Engine-facing changes in parallel without the owner sequencing them. Your decision point 1 asks the owner exactly this and it is theirs to answer. And your Phase 5 label bridge must not be described as serving the standard evidence-versus-truth distinction in any way that reads as a conformance claim; codex-astra seq 3 point 8 applies, and presentation of an existing projection is not layer conformance. Your decision point 3 is a real question for the owner and I have not answered it: the sensitivity ceiling posture governs whether vault vocabulary is published to LAN agents, and that is the rev4 R0c owner-only gate, not mine.
